quality.summary: Only about a third of VitalityScout's 797 servable indexable URLs clearly clear a low-authority YMYL quality bar: 266 clear it, 300 are borderline and need enrichment, and 229 dilute it (106 of those are submitted in the 480-URL sitemap). The guides are the asset. They are 27% of indexable URLs but hold 75% of the site's unique text, and they have almost no near-duplicates (mean pairwise 5-shingle Jaccard 0.012). The dilution comes from four templates: (1) state/city clinic grids that pass a 3-clinic bar with 33–96 truly unique words; (2) single-city state pages that near-duplicate their only city (30 pages, Jaccard 0.42–0.61); (3) med-spa pages built from national-chain stubs and four rotating description templates (LA vs San Diego masked Jaccard 0.974, 0 unique words); (4) 315 provider pages that are indexable but kept out of the sitemap, have a median of 118 unique words, have zero in-content outlinks, and include 74 still marked "Last verified: December 2024". The prior noindex of /traditional-healthcare/* and /health-systems/* was correct (median 93–191 words, 13–60 unique words), but sitewide nav slots still feed it and two other noindexed pages: 9.0% of internal link edges from indexable pages point at noindexed URLs. Causation for Google's "Discovered – currently not indexed" cannot be proven without fresh GSC data. The ED guide itself is substantive (1,262 unique words), so a site-level quality and crawl-demand drag from this inventory is the leading hypothesis, not the page itself.
strengths: Guides are the site's quality core: 214 guides with median 1,964 words and median 1,262 strict-unique words. Mean pairwise 5-shingle Jaccard is 0.012, and only one templated pair (semaglutide-cost and tirzepatide-cost) reaches masked Jaccard 0.5 or higher. They hold 75% of the site's unique text, and all 13 guide URLs with observed Bing or Google traction are in this set. Preserve their URLs, especially /guides/online-ed-treatment.

Weight-loss and hormone-therapy listing descriptions are bespoke rather than templated: no repeated opener dominates even the 258 Texas hormone entries. They include addresses and phone numbers. Pages with 8 or more clinics carry about 945–1,056 non-boilerplate words.

DEXA city pages and cost guides publish dated, sourced price aggregates (e.g. 'Typical DEXA scan cost in Austin: $70 (range $39.95–$185, n=4 clinics, verified July 2026)'). This is the pattern to replicate on other grids and hubs.

The thin-content infrastructure exists and is wired correctly. src/lib/indexability.ts is the single source of truth, the sitemap imports the same threshold, and 0 of the 126 noindexed URLs appear in the sitemap. Raising the bar is a small, safe change.

Noindexing /traditional-healthcare/* and /health-systems/* was the right call (median 93–191 words, 13–60 unique words, 13 impressions and 0 clicks in 100 days), and noindex,follow is confirmed live on /traditional-healthcare/texas.
Destinations (max within-group Jaccard 0.088), FAQ pages, stem-cells pages, longevity regional pages and the 12 local-clinics region pages are distinct, with no near-duplicates.

Live spot checks via Vercel fetch (/med-spa/california/los-angeles, /providers/abbvie, /weight-loss/colorado, /traditional-healthcare/texas) match the build: 200, self-canonical, Link rel=canonical header present. So these build-based findings reflect production.
openQuestions: Bing page-level stats for the 229 DILUTES URLs are not in the baseline, which keeps only the top 12 Bing pages. Before noindexing any group (city grids, providers, single-city states), the owner should export Bing GetPageStats for /weight-loss/*, /hormone-therapy/*, /dexa-scans/*, /med-spa/* and /providers/* to honour the guardrail of keeping URLs that earn clicks.

Without GSC credentials, we cannot see the Page-indexing report split by reason ('Crawled – currently not indexed' vs 'Discovered – currently not indexed') per template. That split is what would confirm or refute the site-level quality hypothesis; per-template sitemaps (quality-1) would make it visible going forward.
Were the 74 provider pages marked 'Last verified: December 2024' actually re-verified with only the label left stale, or are their prices really 22 months old?

The thresholds used here (e.g. at least 5 clinics, at least 250 or 600 unique words, masked Jaccard of 0.4 or 0.5) are heuristics for a low-authority YMYL site. Google publishes no word-count rule, so treat them as a prioritization tool and validate them against post-change indexing transitions.

findings.title: Quality-weighted inventory: 266 of 797 indexable URLs clear the bar, 229 dilute it, and 22% of the sitemap is thin or duplicate
findings.evidence: OBSERVED, from work-quality/classify.mjs, which applies explicit per-template thresholds to spaced re-extracted body text. Method: 5-word shingles, numbers normalized, own city/state/provider-name tokens masked. 'Strict unique' = tokens covered by no shingle that appears on any other prerendered page. Scope: 799 pages have no meta noindex; minus /_not-found and minus /dexa (301 to /dexa-scans in next.config.mjs:8) = 797 servable indexable URLs. Result: CLEARS 266, ENRICH 300, DILUTES 229, UTILITY 2. The 480 sitemap URLs = 266 CLEARS + 106 ENRICH + 106 DILUTES + 2 utility. Sitewide, only 43.5% of indexable body text is strict-unique (384,568 of 883,423 words). Share of URLs vs share of unique text: guides 26.9% vs 75.0%; providers 39.5% vs 9.7%; the 176 state/city grid URLs (weight-loss, hormone-therapy, dexa-scans, med-spa) 22% vs 4.3%. Sanity check: all 18 URLs with observed Bing or Google traction in docs/growth/baseline-2026-09-17.json land in CLEARS or ENRICH; none in DILUTES. Google reported page rows for only 74 URLs in Aug 18–Sep 14, against 797 indexable. /guides/online-ed-treatment (1,771 words, 1,262 unique, nearest-neighbour Jaccard 0.04) is 'Discovered – currently not indexed', so this page is not thin.
findings.impact: HYPOTHESIS: Google rations crawl and index for a young, low-authority YMYL host based partly on site-level quality. With about 529 of 797 URLs below or near the bar, and the most templated ones sitting in the sitemap and nav, Google is unlikely to prioritize crawling the strong guides. This fits the pattern of 5 of 12 sampled priority URLs being 'Discovered – not indexed' while Bing, which is less selective, indexes 792 URLs and sends 936 clicks per 28 days.
findings.recommendation: Apply quality-2 through quality-5 as reversible noindex,follow changes (no deletions). Target: cut indexable URLs from 797 to ≤568 and sitemap URLs from 480 to ≤374. Then promote ENRICH pages only after they pass the thresholds below. Split src/app/sitemap.ts into per-template sitemaps using generateSitemaps (guides, hubs, grids, destinations, providers-if-ever) so the GSC Sitemaps and Page-indexing reports show submitted vs indexed per template. Re-run the same 12-URL inspection sample 3–4 weeks after deploy and record state transitions. Before noindexing any group, export Bing page stats for it to honour the baseline guardrail: keep any URL with Bing clicks.

findings.title: City grid pages with 3–4 clinics pass the MIN_CLINICS_FOR_INDEX=3 bar but carry about 33–96 unique words
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: src/lib/indexability.ts sets MIN_CLINICS_FOR_INDEX = 3, which is a pure clinic-count gate; its own TODO says the richer bar was never built. 54 indexable, in-sitemap city pages list only 3–4 clinics: 24 /weight-loss/*/*, 22 /hormone-therapy/*/*, 8 /dexa-scans/*/*. Medians for these bands: words 558 / 533 / 707; strict-unique words 33 / 34 / 96; share of tokens that is group boilerplate (shingles on ≥50% of group pages) 37% / 38% / 40%. Across all Texas and California city pages, 56–65% of each city page's shingles reappear verbatim on the parent state page (work-quality/statecity.mjs). Worst examples: /weight-loss/arizona/scottsdale (3 clinics, 354 words, 8 unique), /weight-loss/arizona/phoenix (3 clinics, 10 unique), /weight-loss/texas/dallas (3 clinics, 12 unique), /hormone-therapy/california/huntington-beach (3 clinics, 16 unique), /hormone-therapy/texas/dallas (4 clinics, 20 unique), /dexa-scans/california/orange-county (3 clinics, 410 words, 5 unique). Pages with 8 or more clinics are materially better (weight-loss median 121 unique and 945 non-boilerplate words; hormone-therapy 119 and 1,056). Coverage is also skewed: /weight-loss/texas lists Houston 67 but Dallas 3.
findings.impact: Each page is a city-swapped template around a few listing cards whose text is duplicated on the state page. This is the 'thin city grid' pattern the baseline doc says to avoid, and 54 such URLs are actively submitted.
findings.recommendation: In src/lib/indexability.ts, split the gate: index a city page only at ≥5 clinics, and require ≥8 clinics or ≥150 unique words for it to count as a ranking target. The sitemap already imports the same constant, so it updates in step. Result: noindex,follow the 54 pages with 3–4 clinics, which stay live and linked. For the 39 pages with 5–7 clinics (15 weight-loss, 14 hormone-therapy, 10 DEXA), add the DEXA-style dated price aggregate ('Typical X cost in {city}: $N (range, n clinics, verified Mon YYYY)') plus 2–3 city-specific FAQs drawn from the listings. Lift a page back over the bar automatically once its clinic count grows. Fill the big-metro gaps (Dallas, Los Angeles, Phoenix) before adding any new cities.

findings.title: Med-spa city pages are chain-stub doorways built from four rotating description templates
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: /med-spa/california/{los-angeles,san-diego,orange-county,san-francisco} list only 4–5 national chains. Each card reads 'It operates location(s) in the {city} area — use the brand's location finder…' (template at src/data/medspa-chains.ts:159). Within the group, the masked Jaccard for LA vs San Diego is 0.974 (containment 0.99). All four pages have 0–4 strict-unique words and 91–99% group boilerplate. /med-spa/california is 83% boilerplate with 126 unique words. All 200 independent-clinic descriptions use one of four rotating sentence templates ('{name} provides med-spa and aesthetic treatments — botox and dermal fillers — to clients in {city}…', 'Serving {city} and the wider {city} area…', 'Located in {city} in the {city} metro…', '…is a med spa in {town}, serving the greater {city} area'): 150/150 in src/data/medspa-clinics-texas-independents.ts and 50/50 in src/data/medspa-clinics-dfwsa-independents.ts. Resulting pages: /med-spa/texas/fort-worth (16 providers, 82 unique words, 79% boilerplate), /dallas (101 unique, 82%), /san-antonio (86 unique, 78%). The H1 intro at src/app/med-spa/[state]/[city]/page.tsx:157 says 'Listings are national brands serving the metro' even on pages made of independents. gridRobots() counts chain stubs as clinics. Live check via Vercel fetch: /med-spa/california/los-angeles returns 200, self-canonical, no robots meta.
findings.impact: This is the clearest scaled, swapped-noun content on the site, the pattern Google's scaled-content-abuse policy targets. A site-level spam or helpful-content classification would hit the guides too. The template copy also contradicts itself on independent-clinic pages, which hurts trust.
findings.recommendation: Now: noindex,follow and remove from the sitemap the 4 California city pages, /med-spa/california, and /med-spa/texas/{dallas,fort-worth,san-antonio}. In src/app/med-spa/[state]/[city]/page.tsx, exclude national-chain entries from the count passed to gridRobots(). Fix the line-157 intro so it describes the actual mix of listings. Before re-indexing, rewrite each independent's description from verified, clinic-specific facts (injector credentials, published per-unit Botox price with date, services actually listed) and drop the four rotating templates. Keep /med-spa/texas/houston and /med-spa/texas/austin indexable while they are rewritten (709 and 360 unique words).

findings.title: 315 provider pages are indexable but kept out of the sitemap; they are thin, dead ends, partly stale, and partly off-mission
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: /providers/* is 315 of 797 indexable URLs (39.5%) but only 9.7% of the site's unique text. Spaced word count median 356 (the shared inventory undercounts at 292 because texts.jsonl glues adjacent elements). Strict-unique words: p10 68, median 118, max 245; no provider page reaches 250. All 315 have 0 internal in-content outlinks, and 109 have exactly one in-content inbound link. 74 show 'Last verified: December 2024' and 'estimates … as of December 2024'. Live-confirmed on /providers/abbvie: 200, self-canonical, no noindex. The stale set includes the brands that the traffic-earning guides compare: ro-body, function-health, hims-hers-glp1, henry-meds-trt (43 unique words), fountain-trt, everlywell, letsgetchecked, superpower, marek-health, bodyspec, dexafit. 36 pages are off-mission for a cash-pay care directory (13 'Pharmaceutical Companies', 13 'Insurance Companies', 10 'Drug Registries'). src/app/sitemap.ts deliberately omits all providers ('to keep crawl budget on the money pages') while leaving them indexable and self-canonical, which sends mixed signals. Google still discovers them through category and destination listing links (318 from category hubs, 179 from destinations, 44 from guides). Same-entity overlaps with stronger guides: function-health vs /guides/function-health-review (8,756 Bing impressions), ro-body vs /guides/ro-body-weight-loss-cost (5,551), everlywell vs everlywell-review, marek-health vs marek-health-review, bodyspec vs bodyspec-dexa-scan-cost, dexafit vs dexafit-cost.
findings.impact: About 40% of the indexable surface is roughly 120-unique-word profile pages. Some show 22-month-old prices in a YMYL pricing context, contradict the 2026-verified guides on the same brand, and compete with the guides that actually earn traffic.
findings.recommendation: In src/app/providers/[slug]/page.tsx generateMetadata, return NOINDEX_FOLLOW for the 121 below-bar pages: all 36 off-mission entities, the 78 with fewer than 100 unique words, and any still verified in 2024 (7 more). The pages stay live for users and links. For the 6 brand-to-guide pairs above, noindex the provider page and add a prominent 'Full review / cost breakdown' link to the guide. For the remaining 194: re-verify, then raise each to ≥250 unique words (dated price table, what is included, eligibility and state availability, 2–3 alternatives) and add in-content links to the category hub and relevant guides. Put a provider in the sitemap only once it passes that bar. Remove the Insurance, Pharma and Drug-registry provider sets from the directory entirely if they are not part of the cash-pay mandate.

findings.title: 30 single-city state pages near-duplicate their only city, and multi-city state hubs re-render every city's listings
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (work-quality/statecity.mjs): 30 indexable, in-sitemap state pages have exactly one city: 10 /weight-loss/*, 8 /hormone-therapy/*, 12 /dexa-scans/*. Their state-to-city 5-shingle Jaccard is 0.42–0.61, and 73–84% of each state page's shingles appear on its city page. Examples: /weight-loss/colorado vs /denver J 0.57 (state-in-city 0.83); /weight-loss/tennessee vs /nashville 0.61 (0.84); /hormone-therapy/washington-dc vs /washington 0.60 (0.84); /dexa-scans/florida vs /miami 0.50 (0.82). The 30 pages have a median of 653 words and 25 strict-unique words; worst are /dexa-scans/washington-dc (3 unique), /dexa-scans/massachusetts (8), /hormone-therapy/north-carolina (14), /weight-loss/colorado (16). Multi-city hubs dump every city's full cards: /hormone-therapy/texas has 20,229 words and 1,275,650 bytes of HTML; /weight-loss/texas 11,748 words and 670,686 bytes; /weight-loss/california 10,765 words. As a result, 56–65% of each Texas or California city page is duplicated on its state page. Live check: /weight-loss/colorado returns 200, self-canonical, no robots meta.
findings.impact: Two URLs compete for the same listing set in 30 markets, and in the big states the state page cannibalizes and dilutes every city page beneath it. The megapages also cost crawl and render budget (1.28 MB HTML).
findings.recommendation: In src/app/{weight-loss,hormone-therapy,dexa-scans}/[state]/page.tsx and the matching state loops in src/app/sitemap.ts, add a state rule to src/lib/indexability.ts: a state page is indexable only if it has ≥2 indexable cities. Otherwise use noindex,follow, link to the city, and drop it from the sitemap. That covers 30 URLs, and the city stays as the ranking URL. Rebuild multi-city state pages (TX, CA, AZ, FL) as summaries: per city, show the clinic count, the verified median price and the top 3 names, each linking to the city page, instead of full cards. Target: state-to-city containment below 0.2 and HTML under 300 KB.

findings.title: Noindexing traditional-healthcare and health-systems was correct, but sitewide nav still sends equity into noindexed pages
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: the noindex was justified. /traditional-healthcare/* (50 pages) has median 93 words, 13 strict-unique words and 60% boilerplate; /traditional-healthcare/*/* (45) median 191 words, 32 unique; /health-systems/* (21) median 190 words, 60 unique, 49% boilerplate. The layout.tsx comment records 13 impressions and 0 clicks in 100 days. Live: /traditional-healthcare/texas returns 'noindex, follow'. None of the 126 noindexed URLs is in the sitemap. Of the 13 sitewide nav and sidebar targets (excluding /search), 3 are noindexed: top-nav 'By State' goes to /traditional-healthcare (795 pages; src/components/Navigation.tsx:13); sidebar group labels go to /lose-weight and /balance-hormones (797 pages; GROUP_HREF in src/components/SidebarNav.tsx). The sidebar 'Care by State' link goes to /care-by-state (indexable, in the sitemap, 334 words), whose only content links are the 50 noindexed /traditional-healthcare/{state} pages plus /treat-see-doctor, even though its copy promises 'cash-pay clinics… near you'. The homepage links to /traditional-healthcare, /health-systems, /lose-weight and /balance-hormones. 21 hormone city pages link to noindexed /hormone-therapy/texas/san-antonio. Totals: 2,501 of 27,911 internal link edges from indexable pages (9.0%) target noindexed URLs. The best-linked URLs on the site are thin persona hubs (/test-diagnose, /live-longer, /look-better, /treat-see-doctor; 328–359 words; 796–797 inbound each), while substantive hubs get few: /mens-health 1,366 unique words, 84 inbound, 'unknown to Google'; /womens-health 2,017 unique, 78; /mental-health 1,870 unique, 14.
findings.impact: Google tends to treat links into long-term noindexed pages like nofollow, so these three nav slots on about 797 pages pass equity that never returns. Users and crawlers who choose 'By State' land in thin hospital lists rather than the indexable cash-pay state hubs.
findings.recommendation: Keep traditional-healthcare and health-systems noindexed. In SidebarNav GROUP_HREF, point 'lose-weight' to /weight-loss (or /glp1) and 'balance-hormones' to /hormone-therapy (or /trt). In Navigation.tsx:13, point 'By State' to /care-by-state. Rebuild /care-by-state to link to the indexable state hubs (the 14 states × weight-loss, hormone-therapy and dexa-scans after quality-5 pruning, /longevity/{california,florida,new-york,texas}, /med-spa/texas) rather than /traditional-healthcare/*. Drop the homepage links to the noindexed families. Make the 'Other {state} cities' modules skip noindexed cities. Give /mens-health, /womens-health and /mental-health a nav or sidebar slot.

findings.title: DEXA has two URLs per metro (grid page plus cost guide) for 19 cities, plus 12 duplicate state pages
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: each of the 19 /dexa-scans/{state}/{city} grids (410–1,097 words) has a matching /guides/dexa-scan-cost-{city} (1,697–2,165 words) that lists the same clinics. H3 clinic-name overlap is 100% in 12 of 19 pairs (e.g. Austin 6/6, Chicago 6/6, NYC 6/6). The pair cross-link, but their text overlaps little (Jaccard 0.03–0.07), so they compete on intent ('DEXA scan {city}' vs 'DEXA scan cost {city}') rather than as copies. With the 12 single-city DEXA state pages, that makes 52 DEXA local URLs for 19 metros. The guides themselves are a template family: masked Jaccard 0.23–0.31 and heading-set Jaccard up to 0.84 (Boston vs Denver). /guides/dexa-scan-cost-new-york has only 294 strict-unique words. The only Google signal for this cluster is the guide: /guides/dexa-scan-cost-new-york had 48 impressions at average position 5.08 (Aug 18–Sep 14), while /dexa-scans is indexed.
findings.impact: Splitting the same metro intent across two or three URLs halves internal-link and relevance signals. The guide family's shared skeleton also risks a template-level devaluation.
findings.recommendation: Use one ranking URL per metro: keep the cost guide, since it is what Google surfaces and must be preserved. Set the 19 city grids to noindex,follow, or merge each grid's clinic cards into the guide's 'Where to Get a DEXA Scan in {city}' section and 301 grid to guide after the next inspection cycle. Repoint /dexa-scans 'Find near you' links to the guides. Noindex the 12 single-city DEXA states (quality-5). Rewrite each guide's intro, price-driver and FAQ sections with metro-specific facts until masked Jaccard against siblings is below 0.2 and unique words are at least 600; start with new-york, san-diego and boston.

findings.title: Templated 'verified price' guide twins (semaglutide vs tirzepatide, TRT, dental 'prices') and overlapping intent clusters
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (work-quality/guides-masked.mjs): across all 214 guides, masked near-duplication is rare; only one pair is at or above 0.5. That pair is /guides/semaglutide-cost vs /guides/tirzepatide-cost: masked Jaccard 0.717, heading Jaccard 0.83, raw containment 73.5% and 80.5%, with 118 and 83 strict-unique words. /guides/trt-cost (191 unique) is 49% contained in each of them. The same 'What X Actually Run(s)/Charge' template underlies thin companions: /guides/costa-rica-dental-prices (965 words, 286 unique, 41.7% contained in mexico-dental-implant-prices), /guides/mexico-dental-implant-prices (423 unique), /guides/mexico-bariatric-surgery-prices (453), and /guides/dental-implants-abroad-cost-comparison (2,551 words but 404 unique, 41.6% contained in full-mouth-dental-implants-cost-by-country). Overlapping intent clusters by title and H1: semaglutide cost appears across 6 guides (semaglutide-cost, cheapest-way-to-get-semaglutide, compounded-semaglutide, cheapest-glp1-without-insurance, ozempic-cost, wegovy-cost); Turkey hair-transplant cost across 4 (hair-transplant-turkey-cost, hair-transplant-turkey-guide, turkey-hair-transplant-clinics, fue-hair-transplant-istanbul-cost); Costa Rica dental 2; Spain IVF 3 (spain-ivf-cost, spain-fertility-ivf-guide, spain-vs-czech-ivf at 703 words). None of these URLs is in the baseline's Bing or Google traction lists.
findings.impact: These are the guide-level 'near-duplicate guides' the baseline warns about. They split relevance for a high-value GLP-1 cost cluster and add low-unique pages to the strongest template.
findings.recommendation: semaglutide-cost and tirzepatide-cost: either differentiate them (drug-specific dose-step pricing, compounded vs brand rules, Zepbound vials vs Mounjaro pens) until masked Jaccard is below 0.3 and each has at least 600 unique words, or merge both into /guides/cheapest-glp1-without-insurance with 301s and update the 15 and 14 in-content links. Merge costa-rica-dental-prices into costa-rica-dental-guide and dental-implants-abroad-cost-comparison into full-mouth-dental-implants-cost-by-country, with 301s, after confirming in Bing page stats that neither URL has clicks. Add a pre-publish check that fails any new guide whose masked 5-shingle Jaccard against an existing guide is 0.4 or higher, or whose primary query already maps to a guide.

findings.title: Thin and off-mission hubs are promoted from the footer; utility landing pages and two destinations are indexable stubs
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: footer links (src/components/Footer.tsx) reach about 579–601 pages each. findings.impact: Sitewide links concentrate equity on 130–600-word listing stubs and off-topic entity lists. Indexable non-directory landing pages blur the site's topical focus.
findings.recommendation: Noindex /insurance, /pharma, /drug_registry and their providers, and remove them from the footer. Noindex /beta and /centurioncoach (add robots: NOINDEX_FOLLOW in their page metadata). For /vo2max, /orthopedic, /vision, /cardiac, /iv and /allergy, either enrich to the hub bar (8 or more providers, a dated price aggregate, FAQ and a lead-in from the matching guide, about 400 or more unique words) or noindex until then. Meanwhile point the footer 'VO2 Max Testing' link at /guides/vo2-max-test-cost. Expand /destinations/dubai and /cayman-islands to the ~900-word destination template, or fold them into /medical-tourism.

findings.title: Visible staleness on YMYL pricing pages: 30 guide titles still say 2024 or 2025 next to 2026-verified siblings
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (inventory titles): of 214 guides, 143 carry '2026' in the title, 16 carry '2024' and 14 carry '2025'. Guides hold 75% of unique text, and every observed traction URL is a guide or hub: allergy-testing-cost at Bing position 3.26, lasik-cost-usa at 7.0 with 26 clicks, mri-cost-without-insurance at 5.0, and Google indexes the labs cluster. onpage.summary: The basic on-page structure is solid: every page has exactly one H1, and none of the 798 indexable prerendered pages has a missing or duplicate meta description. Guide titles mostly lead with the query and carry real price anchors. The SERP-snippet layer has three problems with strong evidence behind them. (1) On Sep 19 (b1e6e6b), after the Bing window in which its CTR rose from 0.69% to 8.26%, the title and description of the #1 traffic page (/guides/online-ed-treatment) were replaced with a longer, generic version. This was not documented, and no data has been collected since. (2) The pages with the most impressions turn them into clicks very poorly: Function Health 0.14% at position 7, against LASIK's 3.30% at the same position; Ro 0.61%; MRI 0.60%, down from 1.61% at a stable position. Function's problem is mainly a brand-navigation query, so a title rewrite can only help so much. (3) Freshness is visibly decaying. 34 titles still say 2024 or 2025, and 126 pages show 'verified/updated December 2024' stamps. 153 titles hard-code '2026' across 152 source files, so they will all go stale on Jan 1, 2027. Template-level issues add to this: a ' | VitalityScout' suffix pushes 271 titles past 65 characters; 795 of 798 pages inherit the homepage og:title, og:description and og:url, with no og:image anywhere; and the category-hub and provider templates produce thin, sometimes misleading or duplicated snippets. Limits: no Bing or Google data exists after Sep 15, and no Bing query rows exist for Ro, LASIK, allergy or full-body MRI. CTR causes and the effect of the Sep 19 change are therefore hypotheses until fresh data is pulled.
strengths: Exactly one H1 on every page, and no missing or duplicate meta descriptions across 798 indexable prerendered pages.

Guide titles use title.absolute without the brand suffix (average 56 characters; only 22 of 214 exceed 65). They lead with the query phrase and carry concrete price anchors, e.g. 'Quest vs Labcorp Prices (2026): Self-Pay From $29', where title and H1 match exactly.
Title, H1 and slug line up closely on all 8 pages with 300+ Bing impressions. The low CTR is not caused by a keyword mismatch.

The ED page is a freshness model to copy: a visible 'Prices checked September 17, 2026' byline, cited sources (ED_SOURCES), and Article dateModified tied to the ED_VERIFIED_AT constant in src/lib/ed-offers.ts. Do not change its URL or H1.
Priority guides show 'Last updated: June 2026' and carry MedicalWebPage + FAQPage JSON-LD.
The homepage WebSite JSON-LD declares name 'VitalityScout', which supports Google's separate site-name display, so the brand suffix can safely be dropped from long titles.
796 pages have correct self-canonicals, and the deliberate noindex on /traditional-healthcare/* and /health-systems/* keeps thin pages out of the index. Keep both.
The /dexa to /dexa-scans 308 consolidation (next.config.mjs:8) is in place.
openQuestions: No Bing or Google data exists after Sep 15, 2026, so the effect of the Sep 19 ED title change cannot be measured. Pull Bing GetPageStats/GetQueryStats for /guides/online-ed-treatment for the Sep 19 to Oct 18 buckets before making further changes.

Which titles do Bing and Google actually display for the priority URLs (title rewriting), and what do the competing SERPs for 'mri cost without insurance' and 'ro weight loss' look like? A manual SERP review is needed before blaming titles for low MRI CTR, as the baseline doc warns.
Bing has no query rows for Ro, LASIK, allergy or full-body MRI. How much of Ro's 5,551 impressions come from brand-navigation queries such as 'ro weight loss' or 'ro body'?
Can verified offer data still support the '$20-$90/mo' range from the old ED title, or should the restored title rely only on brand names?

Does VitalityScout have referral or affiliate relationships with Function, Ro or Hims? That decides whether words like 'independent' may appear in snippets. The rewrites above deliberately leave it out.

By template: /providers/* 109 over 65 (max 111c: 'Amazon One Medical (On-Demand Care) — Online Doctor & Urgent Care Provider | VitalityScout'); /hormone-therapy/*/* 49 of 49 and /hormone-therapy/* 14 of 14 ('Phoenix TRT & HRT Clinics: 4 Hormone Therapy Options | VitalityScout'); /dexa-scans/* 14 of 14; /weight-loss/* and /weight-loss/*/* 20; /local-clinics/* 14 of 14; /med-spa/*/* 9 of 9; /faq/* 4 of 4; /guides/* 22 (guides use title.absolute and no suffix; max 78c). findings.recommendation: Title policy: the full title is 60 characters or fewer and about 575px or narrower. Put the query phrase first, then a concrete differentiator (price, count, named options). Add the brand only when it fits: create a seoTitle(base) helper in src/lib/seo.ts that returns base + ' | VitalityScout' when the total is 60 characters or fewer, and otherwise {absolute: base}. Use it in the generateMetadata of hormone-therapy/[state] (line 33), [state]/[city] (55), dexa-scans/[state] (33) and [city] (80), weight-loss/[state] (37) and [city] (56), med-spa/[state]/[city] (100), local-clinics/*, providers/[slug] (27) and [category] (44). indexation.summary: Nothing technical is stopping Google from indexing the site. Live checks on 20 URLs (the full 12-URL Google inspection sample, 5 random /providers/* pages and 3 random city pages) all came back 200, with no redirect, a self-referencing canonical in both the HTML and the Link header, no meta robots, no X-Robots-Tag, and the H1 and prices present in the server HTML. The live sitemap is byte-identical to the local build: 480 URLs, every one a 200 indexable self-canonical page. Pages Google has indexed and pages it has not look technically the same, so the 'Discovered – currently not indexed' state is a crawl-priority and site-quality problem. The biggest fixes are structural. First, shrink the low-value indexable inventory: 315 /providers/* pages are indexable and internally linked but left out of the sitemap, and many are thin, stale or off-topic. Second, stop the sitewide navigation sending link equity to noindexed hubs. Third, do the cheap owner actions in Search Console and Bing: request indexing, re-read the sitemap status, automate IndexNow. Smaller problems: www.vitalityscout.com is not attached to the Vercel project, so it cannot redirect to the apex. The sitemap has no lastmod even though 441 of its 480 pages carry a dateModified. /search is an indexable page rendered fresh for every query. /dexa is still linked from 48 pages. On coverage, from this lens: don't open new URL families (city grids, provider pages) until the priority URLs leave 'Discovered'. Expand by deepening clusters Google already indexes (labs, DEXA) and the pages with Bing traction.
strengths: Live robots.txt returns 200, allows all, declares the sitemap and blocks no rendering assets. No X-Robots-Tag on any fetched URL.

Live sitemap.xml (480 URLs) is byte-identical to the build. Every URL is a 200 indexable self-canonical page, with no noindexed or redirected entries. The ≥3-clinic index bar is shared between the templates and the sitemap through src/lib/indexability.ts. There is no fake build-time lastmod.
Self-canonical rel=canonical on all indexable pages, plus a matching Link header. The .vercel.app production alias returns 308 to the apex (observed live).
Main content is server-rendered: H1, prices and provider lists are in the SSR HTML on all 20 sampled URLs. The client-side bailout template sits after </main> on all 925 pages.

Real 404 status across all route types (/[category], /providers/[slug], static), with no soft-404 templates. Case variants return 404, a trailing slash returns 308 to the non-slash URL, and no internal links carry query strings, so there are no duplicate URL variants.
/dexa and /destinations are permanent 308 redirects to /dexa-scans and /medical-tourism. /destinations has 0 internal links.

The noindex,follow pruning is deliberate and consistent: 95 traditional-healthcare pages, 21 health-systems pages, 7 thin grid cities and 2 persona hubs are all excluded from the sitemap and still crawlable.
Production is current with main (ab5f870). The ED guide's URL and H1 were preserved, as the baseline requires.

Has Bing Webmaster recorded a recent sitemap fetch, and which of the two IndexNow keys was used for the Sep 19 submission?

findings.title: The sitemap is valid but carries no lastmod even though 441 of 480 pages already have a JSON-LD dateModified; priority and changefreq are uniform
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: live /sitemap.xml returns 200, application/xml, x-vercel-cache HIT, age 26 days, no X-Robots-Tag. It has 480 <loc>, byte-identical to .next/server/app/sitemap.xml.body. All 480 are prerendered, indexable and self-canonical, and none is noindexed or redirected. There are 0 <lastmod>. changefreq/priority pairs: weekly/0.8 on 227 URLs, monthly/0.6 on 144, monthly/0.7 on 58, weekly/0.9 on 30, monthly/0.8 on 20, weekly/1 on 1. Of the 480 sitemap pages, 441 have a JSON-LD dateModified (19 distinct dates, not build-time stamps). Use it for both the JSON-LD dateModified and lastModified in src/app/sitemap.ts, so the dates stay accurate and update only on substantive edits. Fix the MRI guide's date. changefreq and priority can be dropped (harmless either way). Keep the current rule that noindexed and redirected URLs never enter the sitemap.

schema.summary: The structured data is syntactically clean: 0 JSON-LD parse errors across 803 pages with markup, and every @type and property validates against schema.org (schema-dts 2.1.0) except TravelGuide, which is not a schema.org type, and one stray property. No aggregateRating or Review markup exists anywhere. Structured data does not explain Google's indexing gap: the "Discovered – currently not indexed" URLs have not been fetched yet, so no markup on them has been read. Treat this lens as trust and hygiene work, not as an indexing lever. The serious problems are about accuracy, which matters on health (YMYL) pages: 144 MedicalWebPage blocks claim reviewedBy "VitalityScout Editorial Team", which the site's own /editorial-policy contradicts. All 315 /providers/* pages, including Pfizer, UnitedHealthcare and the FDA's own databases, are typed MedicalBusiness (a LocalBusiness subtype), and 129 of them have no address at all. Template-wide hardcoded dateModified values disagree with the "verified Jul 2026" dates shown on the same pages. Beyond accuracy, there are gaps in the site-level entity setup: there is no Organization node, the Article publisher logo returns 404 in production, no Article has an image, and BreadcrumbList is on 43 of about 799 indexable pages even though 242 pages already show a breadcrumb trail.
strengths: Zero aggregateRating, Review or Rating nodes in any JSON-LD, despite 880 third-party rating fields in src/data. This complies with Google's review-snippet rules; keep it that way.

0 JSON-LD parse errors across 803 pages with markup. Every @type and property validates against the schema.org vocabulary (schema-dts 2.1.0) except TravelGuide, SearchAction query-input (a Google extension, fine) and one medicalSpecialty.
183 of 200 FAQPage blocks mirror the visible Q&A verbatim, mostly through the shared buildFAQSchema in src/lib/jsonLd.ts (172 files).

The Price Index Dataset and the ED guide take their dates from data (indexAsOf, ED_VERIFIED_AT). The ED guide's Article author 'VitalityScout research' matches /editorial-policy. Use these as the model for every template.
146 pages carry citation arrays (845 sources) that match visible 'Sources & References' sections. All 140 MedicalWebPage.mainEntity -> FAQPage @id references resolve on-page.
No affiliate or tracking parameters in any of the 997 external URLs in the JSON-LD; schema URLs point to official provider pages.
Live production serves the same JSON-LD as the local build (checked /providers/pfizer). Middleware adds a Link rel=canonical header, and the home WebSite name is consistent ('VitalityScout').
openQuestions: Is there a real, named person (the owner as editor, or a licensed clinician) willing to be shown as author or reviewer with a bio page? Without one, Person author and reviewedBy markup must stay off per /editorial-policy.
Are there official brand profiles (LinkedIn, X, Crunchbase) to list in Organization.sameAs?

Should the 36 non-provider entities (13 insurers, 13 pharma companies, 10 drug or government databases) stay as /providers/* pages in a cash-pay directory at all? Removing or noindexing them is simpler than re-typing them.

No GSC credentials are available, so I could not check the Enhancements reports (Breadcrumbs, FAQ, Dataset, Unparsable structured data) or whether Google has parsed markup on the 6 indexed sample URLs. That data would confirm the impact of schema-4, schema-5 and schema-6.

The repo clone is shallow (history from 2026-06-25). Earlier dates were checked only for the weight-loss city template via the GitHub API; true first-publish dates for the 29 round-dated guides need GitHub history.

findings.title: reviewedBy 'VitalityScout Editorial Team' and lastReviewed on 144 YMYL pages are invisible, unbacked, and contradict the site's own editorial policy
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: 144 MedicalWebPage blocks carry reviewedBy {Organization 'VitalityScout Editorial Team'} plus lastReviewed (141 guide page.tsx files, plus src/app/[category]/page.tsx:160-161 (/dexa), src/app/trt/page.tsx:103-104 and src/app/price-index/page.tsx:319-320); find them with `grep -rln reviewedBy src`. On all 145 pages that have lastReviewed, it equals dateModified, so it records the authoring date, not a separate review. The phrase 'Editorial Team' appears in the visible body text of 0 pages (texts.jsonl). No Person reviewer exists anywhere (hasAuthorPerson = 0). /editorial-policy (published 2026-09-17) states: '"VitalityScout research" ... does not mean the page has been reviewed by a clinician. A clinical review is identified only when an actual reviewer and credentials are displayed.' The newer ED guide follows that policy (Article, author 'VitalityScout research', no reviewedBy). The 141 older guides do not; these include priority URLs /guides/mri-cost-without-insurance, /guides/full-body-mri-scan-cost and /guides/quest-vs-labcorp-pricing.
findings.impact: On a MedicalWebPage, reviewedBy plus lastReviewed claims a medical review took place. Google's structured-data policies forbid marking up content that is not visible and content that misrepresents the page. On YMYL pages this is the kind of signal that can lead to a manual action or a site-level loss of trust. It also contradicts the site's published policy, which raters and AI answer engines can read. There is no rich-result upside to keeping it, because MedicalWebPage has no Google search feature.
findings.recommendation: Delete reviewedBy and lastReviewed from all 144 blocks now. Keep dateModified. The fix is a mechanical edit across the files `grep -rln reviewedBy src` returns, plus [category], trt and price-index. Re-add them only for a real, named reviewer who is shown on the page, as the editorial policy requires. For example: "reviewedBy":{"@type":"Person","name":"<real name>, MD","url":"https://vitalityscout.com/reviewers/<slug>","hasCredential":{"@type":"EducationalOccupationalCredential","credentialCategory":"MD"}},"lastReviewed":"<actual review date>". Also show a visible 'Medically reviewed by …' line, generated from the same data. Until then, use the ED guide's pattern: author 'VitalityScout research', no reviewedBy.

findings.title: All 315 /providers/* pages use MedicalBusiness (a LocalBusiness subtype), including pharma companies, insurers, FDA/NIH databases and telehealth brands; 129 have no address
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: src/lib/jsonLd.ts buildProviderSchema() hardcodes '@type':'MedicalBusiness' for every provider. Provider data (transpiled from src/lib/providers*.ts) breaks down as: 13 insurers (UnitedHealthcare, Aetna…), 13 pharma companies (Pfizer, Eli Lilly…), 10 drug registries (Drugs@FDA, FDA Orange Book, DailyMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, GoodRx…), 74 telehealth_national/state_limited brands, 21 hybrid, 40 in_person_local, and 180 in_person_destination clinics (179 outside the US). Of the 315 MedicalBusiness nodes, 129 have no address, 186 have no streetAddress, and 7 have no addressCountry. Example: /providers/panama-city-surgery-center has addressLocality 'Panama City' with no country, but the data says 'Panama City, FL', so it can be confused with Panama City, Panama, a destination the site covers. Live https://vitalityscout.com/providers/pfizer serves {"@type":"MedicalBusiness","name":"Pfizer","hasCredential":[{"credentialCategory":"FDA approved"}…],"priceRange":"Varies by drug"}. The node also has no @id and no WebPage wrapper, and the VitalityScout page itself is not described. 11 priceRange strings are over 100 characters (max 175). /telehealth also types the site's own directory as a MedicalBusiness ('Telehealth Services Directory').
findings.impact: This is a correctness and trust problem, not a ranking lever. Google's LocalBusiness markup expects a physical business with an address. These nodes are ignored or flagged, and they describe a pharma company or a government database as a local medical business. The 315 pages are about 40% of the indexable URL set, so the inaccuracy repeats at scale on thin pages (avg 292 words) that are already weak.
findings.recommendation: Change buildProviderSchema to choose the type from category and deliveryModel. Add an optional `schemaType` override field to Provider in src/lib/types.ts. Mapping: insurance and pharma (26) → 'Corporation'. drug_registry (10) → no business type; use a WebPage whose about is {"@type":"Dataset" or "WebSite","name":…,"publisher":{"@type":"GovernmentOrganization","name":"U.S. Food and Drug Administration"}}, or drop these from /providers entirely. Telehealth (about 65) → 'MedicalOrganization'. Multi-location US chains such as BodySpec, RadNet and IV franchises (about 28) → 'MedicalOrganization'. Destination clinics → 'Dentist' (about 42), 'Hospital' (about 22, names containing Hospital), 'MedicalClinic' (about 116). Use ISO addressCountry codes and fill addressRegion for US cities. Wrap each node in an @graph like this: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://vitalityscout.com/providers/pfizer#webpage","url":"https://vitalityscout.com/providers/pfizer","name":"Pfizer — Pharma Provider","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://vitalityscout.com/#website"},"about":{"@id":"https://vitalityscout.com/providers/pfizer#entity"},"dateModified":"<provider.lastVerified>"},{"@type":"Corporation","@id":"https://vitalityscout.com/providers/pfizer#entity","name":"Pfizer","url":"https://www.pfizer.com","description":"…"}]}. Put accreditations in hasCredential only as {"@type":"EducationalOccupationalCredential","name":"JCI accreditation","recognizedBy":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Joint Commission International"}}, and only when the accreditation has been verified. Drop credentials like 'FDA approved' attached to a company.

findings.title: Hardcoded template dateModified values contradict visible 'verified' dates and git history; 55 sitemap URLs carry pre-2026 dates
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (git history is shallow, back to 2026-06-25; older history from the GitHub API): (a) src/app/weight-loss/[state]/[city]/page.tsx:95 and [state]/page.tsx:82 hardcode dateModified '2026-02-01'. The same value appears on 69 weight-loss and 63 hormone-therapy pages. The weight-loss city template was created 2026-02-02 and received verified pricing on 2026-07-12 (+29 lines) and 2026-07-21. /weight-loss/texas/houston shows 'verified from clinic site · Jul 2026' while its JSON-LD says 2026-02-01. (b) med-spa (12 pages) hardcode 2026-06-13, but the city template changed on 2026-07-21 (+85 and +28 lines) and /med-spa/texas/dallas shows 'Jul 2026'. dexa-scans (33 pages) hardcode 2026-06-10, but the template changed on 2026-07-12 (+30). (c) src/app/destinations/[destination]/page.tsx:928 hardcodes '2024-12-21' on 14 pages, but the template gained provider tables on 2026-06-25 (+69) and 2026-07-13. (d) /guides/compounded-semaglutide has schema datePublished = dateModified = 2025-01-01 and visible 'Last updated: January 2025', yet its text describes the FDA's February 2025 shortage resolution, so the date is demonstrably wrong. In total, 55 sitemap URLs (36 guides, 14 destinations, 5 longevity) declare dateModified before 2026, and 29 guides use round placeholder datePublished values (16× '2024-12-01', 13× '2025-01-01'). By contrast, guide-level hardcoded dates track commits to within ±2 days (only 14 of 213 have a substantive commit after the declared date).
findings.impact: Mismatched dates on YMYL pricing pages weaken trust. Google uses structured and visible dates in snippets and to judge freshness. Stale 2024 dates on medical-tourism and GLP-1 pages tell searchers the content is out of date. Hardcoded constants also mean the dates never move when the data does. The sitemap has no <lastmod> (sitemap.json), so the site sends no reliable freshness signal anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Add src/lib/page-dates.ts and make it the single source for dateModified in JSON-LD, the visible 'Updated' line, and sitemap <lastmod> (src/app/sitemap.ts). For city, state and destination templates, compute the max of clinic lastVerified and pricing asOf for that page's rows. src/app/price-index/page.tsx already does this with indexAsOf; copy that pattern. For guides, keep explicit dates, but add a CI check that fails when a guide's page.tsx changes by 15 or more lines without a dateModified bump. Fix compounded-semaglutide's dates, then review it for content. Leave untouched 2024 pages honestly dated, but queue them for content refresh rather than bumping dates without a real change.

findings.title: FAQPage on 200 pages earns no Google rich results; 17 pages have schema Q&A that differs from the visible Q&A
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (faqcheck.mjs over all 200 FAQPage pages, not just a sample): 183 pages mirror every question and answer verbatim (1,108 questions in total; most built with buildFAQSchema in src/lib/jsonLd.ts). 12 guides hand-write a separate faqJsonLd that does not match the visible FAQ: 35 of 57 questions are not on the page as written, and the answers are longer. Example: /guides/hungary-dental-cost Q1 schema answer is 530 characters, while the visible answer is about 230 characters with different wording. Affected guides: brazil-plastic-surgery-cost, colombia-plastic-surgery-cost, costa-rica-cosmetic-surgery-cost, czech-ivf-cost, hungary-dental-cost, korea-plastic-surgery-cost, los-algodones-reviews, panama-dental-cost, spain-ivf-cost, stem-cell-knees-mexico, stem-cell-therapy-cost, thailand-cosmetic-surgery-cost. The 5 /faq pages (src/app/faq/page.tsx and the glp1, hair-transplant, labs, medical-tourism subpages) pass condensed answer strings to buildFAQSchema that differ from the richer visible <details> answers (38 answers). Duplication across pages is low: 15 questions repeat, mostly the DEXA city guides.
findings.impact: Since August 2023, Google shows FAQ rich results only for well-known government and health authority sites. As of mid-2026 that limit still applies as far as I know, and VitalityScout does not qualify, so the Google benefit is about zero. The remaining value is with Bing, which drives 936 clicks per 28 days, and with AI answer extraction. That value is real but small, and it depends on the markup matching the page. On the 17 drifting pages, the structured data includes text that is not visible, which breaks Google's content guidelines and grows with every edit.
findings.recommendation: Keep FAQPage where it mirrors the page exactly, since it costs little and helps Bing. Fix the 17 pages by keeping one `const FAQS=[{question,answer}]` array per page and rendering both the visible list and buildFAQSchema(FAQS) from it. A shared <FaqSection items={FAQS}/> component that outputs both makes drift impossible. Add a build-time check that every Question.name appears in the rendered HTML. Do not add FAQ blocks to new templates purely for schema, and do not expect Google FAQ snippets in reporting.

findings.title: BreadcrumbList on only 43 of about 799 indexable pages, though 242 pages already render a visible multi-level trail
findings.evidence: OBSERVED (bc.mjs over the built HTML): 43 pages have BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, each written inline in its own page.tsx; there is no shared component in src/components or src/lib. 242 indexable pages render a visible trail without the markup: 84 guides with a 'Home / Guides / …' text trail, 3 guides with aria breadcrumbs (e.g. /guides/bluechew-cost), 55 /weight-loss/*/*, 49 /hormone-therapy/*/*, 19 /dexa-scans/*/*, 9 /med-spa/*/*, 14 /local-clinics/*, and 9 compare hubs (/mens-health, /cgm, /skincare…). Another 354 pages have only a '← Back to X' link: 315 providers, 14 destinations, 21 guides and 4 /faq pages. About 64 guides have no trail at all.
findings.impact: BreadcrumbList is one of the few Google rich results this site is eligible for. It shows on desktop results; since January 2025 mobile results show only the domain. It also gives Google and Bing an explicit hierarchy, which matters while Google is still deciding which of 480 sitemap URLs to crawl. 315 provider pages that are absent from the sitemap would gain a machine-readable parent.
findings.recommendation: Create src/components/Breadcrumbs.tsx taking items:{name,href}[]. It should render the visible <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> and the matching JSON-LD from the same array: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":"https://vitalityscout.com/"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"Weight Loss","item":"https://vitalityscout.com/weight-loss"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":3,"name":"Texas","item":"https://vitalityscout.com/weight-loss/texas"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":4,"name":"Houston"}]}. Roll it out to these templates first: src/app/providers/[slug]/page.tsx (Home > {category.name} > {provider.name}), weight-loss, hormone-therapy, dexa-scans and med-spa [state] and [city], destinations/[destination], CompareCategoryPage.tsx, then the guides. Replace the 43 inline copies.

findings.title: Article markup on 56 guides has no image and no Person author; 29 use placeholder datePublished values
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: 56 Article blocks plus 11 MedicalWebPage blocks with a headline have image = 0. Authors are Organization only: 64× 'VitalityScout' and 3× 'VitalityScout research'. Publishers: 45 name-only, plus 22 with the 404 logo (see schema-4). datePublished counts: 2024-12-01 ×16, 2025-01-01 ×13, 2025-01-03 ×1; for the post-graft guides bluechew-cost and sildenafil-cost-without-insurance, datePublished 2026-09-17 is 2 days before their first commit (2026-09-19). Reference it as "image":["https://vitalityscout.com/guides/<slug>/opengraph-image"] and set the matching og:image. findings.title: Price Index Dataset is valid but missing license, distribution and spatialCoverage
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: /price-index carries a Dataset (@id …/price-index#dataset) with name, description, creator, publisher, creditText, isAccessibleForFree, temporalCoverage '2026-07-21', measurementTechnique and 10 PropertyValue variableMeasured entries. findings.title: 132 city grid pages use bare MedicalWebPage, although they hold real addresses and verified prices; third-party ratings must never become aggregateRating
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: /weight-loss/*/* (55), /hormone-therapy/*/* (49), /dexa-scans/*/* (19) and /med-spa/*/* (9) emit only MedicalWebPage {name, description, author, dateModified}, with no about, url or item list. The data has real visible street addresses: WeightLossClinic.address is required (src/lib/weightloss-clinic-types.ts:10), e.g. '7373 Old Katy Rd #150, Houston, TX 77024' shown on /weight-loss/texas/houston. findings.impact: This is the one template where local-business markup would be accurate. An ItemList of addressed MedicalClinic entities improves entity understanding for Bing, Google and AI engines on the city 'near me' pages. It is not a rich-result guarantee, since Google's carousels do not cover clinics. Copying the Google or Yelp star ratings into aggregateRating would break Google's review-snippet rules (no ratings aggregated from other sites) and risk a manual action.
findings.recommendation: In the four [city] templates, add an ItemList of clinics that have an address: {"@type":"ItemList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"item":{"@type":"MedicalClinic","name":"…","url":"<clinic.website>","telephone":"<if present>","address":{"@type":"PostalAddress","streetAddress":"7373 Old Katy Rd #150","addressLocality":"Houston","addressRegion":"TX","postalCode":"77024","addressCountry":"US"}}}]}.
